vedic_reference.note: Janmajeya is the name of a king in the Mahabharata who was a great-grandson of the Pandava king Arjuna.

data.cultural_impact: This name holds deep cultural significance, as it suggests a strong and auspicious beginning. In Hindu mythology, the divine name or 'Sabda Brahman' holds considerable importance, and Janmajeya can be seen as a celebration of this concept. If someone holds this name, it might be perceived that they are blessed with divine grace, and have been triumphant from the very moment of their birth.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Janmajeya is a name that embodies the concept of 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam'. The victory referred to in 'Janmajeya' isn't mere worldly success, but a spiritual triumph. It implies the attainment of self-realization and enlightenment from the very beginning of one's life. This name signifies the belief that each individual is an integral part of the universe, and striving for self-improvement and personal growth, one can embody the victory of the soul over the body and passions. This spiritual significance adds depth to the name, instilling a sense of determination and commitment towards their spiritual journey.

historical_references.reference: Janmajeya was a king of the Shakyas, an ancient Indian tribe. He is mentioned in the Buddhist Jataka tales as a contemporary of the Buddha.
historical_references.context: Janmajeya ruled over the Shakyas during the time of the Buddha, around 500 BCE.

historical_references.reference: The story of Janmajeya's death is told in the Mahabharata, where it is said that he was killed by the Kshatriya hero Bhima during the Kurukshetra War.
historical_references.context: Janmajeya's death occurs during the great battle between the Pandava and Kaurava clans, which takes place in the Indian epic Mahabharata.
